help.stock: Stock details are optional. Add a stock name, supplier, received date, or stock expenses only when you want more complete purchasing and audit records.
help.products: Think of products as Group → Variety → Item. Example: iPhone 15 Pro Max → Silver 256 GB → each phone's IMEI. Use Quantity when matching stock is counted together.
help.catalog: A product group keeps the same main product together. Each variety is one version inside that group, and individual items can carry their own identifiers.
help.record: Quantity is how much stock you received. Buying cost is what you paid and does not change the product variety. For individually tracked stock, add each item's IMEI, serial number, or other identifier.
help.review: Check the products you recorded, then save a draft or receive the stock. Optional stock details are included only when you entered them.
help.familyAssignment: A product group keeps related versions of the same product together. Example: iPhone 15 Pro Max is the group; Silver 256 GB and Black 512 GB are different varieties inside it.
help.autoSku: A variety is one version inside a product group. Example: Silver · 256 GB. Fill in what makes this version different. Use Quantity for stock counted together, or Individual when each item needs its own IMEI or serial number. Tunakuza handles the SKU automatically.
help.existingSku: A variety is one exact version inside a product group, such as Silver 256 GB. Select it if it already exists; otherwise add a new variety.
help.existingCategory: Choose the product group first. Then use an existing variety or add another variety inside the same group. Example: iPhone 15 Pro Max → Silver 256 GB.
help.newCategory: A product group is the main product people recognize, for example iPhone 15 Pro Max. After creating the group, add its first variety, for example Silver 256 GB.
help.uncategorized: Use this quick path when you only want a simple product record and do not want to set up a product group now. You can still record it by quantity or track each item separately.
